target_audience.core_avatar: A 19-year-old university student or young professional who goes to the gym, listens to ambient or phonk music, spends time on YouTube Shorts and TikTok, wants to become more disciplined, sometimes feels isolated or uncertain about the future, and actively looks for content that helps them grow mentally and emotionally.
share_triggers: This is exactly how I feel.

weekly_batch_mode.description: As of 2026-07-27, the owner requested a fully autonomous weekly batch: every Monday, script/produce/gate all 21 shorts and 7 long-form videos for that week in one cycle, then upload all of them immediately but with YouTube's scheduled-publish feature (privacyStatus=private + publishAt) so they actually go live spread across the week at the slot times below, rather than all going public on Monday. See agents/0_orchestrator.md 'Weekly batch cycle' for the full operating logic.
weekly_batch_mode.slot_time_note: Local times in the timezone above (Europe/London); convert to UTC accounting for BST/GMT when computing each video's publishAt timestamp. Long-form is scheduled after the day's 3rd short so a viewer's day has short-form energy first, calm ambient content in the evening.
weekly_batch_mode.batch_scale_warning: 28 full pipeline cycles (scout->script->produce->gate->publish) in a single run is a large amount of work — real risk of hitting session/token/time limits mid-batch (this has already happened once in a much smaller single-day session). The weekly trigger fires into a persistent, pre-existing session that already has repo access (a fresh session per firing was tried first and failed a live test run: it had no repo clone and no add_repo tool available to get one, since MCP/connector tools aren't passed to fresh-session routine firings). state/weekly_batch_progress.json tracks completion per-item so an interrupted run can be resumed from where it left off rather than restarting the whole batch, and sub-agents should be used liberally within the run to keep the parent session's own context budget from being the limiting factor.
weekly_batch_mode.upload_quota_warning: 2026-07-27T21:35Z: uploading ~11 videos within about an hour of wall-clock time hit YouTube's daily upload quota (HTTP 400 uploadLimitExceeded), even though each video's scheduled_publish_at (via the API's publishAt scheduling) was spread across the week — publishAt only controls when a video goes public, not when the upload call itself counts against the daily cap. Fixed by decoupling production (script/produce/gate, no per-day limit) from publishing (throttled to ~4 uploads/day matching shorts_per_day+long_form_per_day, driven by a trigger that now fires daily instead of weekly). See agents/0_orchestrator.md's Weekly batch cycle section for the full two-phase model.

operating_budget: Claude Pro subscription usage only; no paid third-party APIs
human_approval_note: No manual approval step exists in this pipeline. Automatic gates (config/gates.json) replace human review. Gates are never weakened to hit the publishing schedule; failing items are quarantined and the next candidate is selected instead.

short_form_style_guidance.pacing: Fast cuts locked to the actual beat of the audio track (real beat detection, not a fixed-interval grid), HARD CAP of 1.5 seconds per individual shot regardless of beat spacing (tightened from 2.0s per owner direction, 2026-07-27). Pick upbeat/fast-tempo audio deliberately BECAUSE it drives the cut pace — a faster song produces closer-together beats and therefore quicker, more energetic cuts; a slow track would force fewer/slower cuts even with the cap in place. Total video length is now 8-12 seconds (tightened from ~27s per owner direction, 2026-07-27) — at that length a video is roughly 6-9 distinct cuts, not 18-20. The audio's own slow/quiet intro is detected and skipped so playback opens on the real hook/drop, not a build-up — a viewer scrolling onto the Short should land on the energetic part immediately.
short_form_style_guidance.energy: High-energy, upbeat, aggressive. Sound must be fast-tempo (phonk, hardtekk, reggaeton, aggressive trap/drill, uptempo mixes) — this is what's actually trending for gym/discipline/motivation shorts per real competitor research (2026), not a stylistic guess. NEVER use slow ambient/piano/meditation/rain tracks for short-form — those belong to long-form only. If a candidate's angle is genuinely 'quiet/silent' in theme, the visual pacing must still stay fast (quick cuts) even if the music is sparse — 'quiet' is a lyrical/thematic concept, not permission to slow the edit down.
short_form_style_guidance.visual_grade: Dark, moody, low-exposure color grade ('gymcore' aesthetic) — reduced brightness/exposure, boosted contrast, slightly desaturated or cool-toned. This is a real, currently-trending look for this niche, not just a preference.
short_form_style_guidance.text_rules: NO on-screen text/captions — dropped entirely per owner direction (2026-07-27). This is a pure visual+audio edit; the title/description carry the message instead.
short_form_style_guidance.sources_note: Based on live web research into trending gym/motivation/phonk shorts content and general 2026 YouTube Shorts editing/retention best practices — see state/performance_notes.json for the full findings and sources.

long_form_style_guidance.pacing: Slow, calm, minimal/no cuts — a single looping ambient scene, not edited for pace at all.
long_form_style_guidance.energy: Calm, ambient, meditative. Slow piano/pad/rain/nature tracks belong here, never in short-form.
long_form_style_guidance.visual_grade: Warm or cool moody ambient tones per the scene (rain-on-window, fireplace, etc.), not the dark low-exposure short-form grade — long-form should read as a calm background, not an energetic edit.
